author: Augustine of Hippo
disclaimer: Contrast summaries only — full Augustine works are not yet in this library. Readings are editorial, for comparison on the timeline.

points.summary: After Adam, the will is not free to turn to God for salvation without prior grace; choice alone cannot restore what was lost.
points.citation: Contrast card (late Augustine on grace and the will)

points.summary: Infants inherit a guilt and mortality tied to Adam’s sin; baptism remits that original guilt.
Grace does not merely assist an already willing person; it must precede and enable the will’s good turn.
Faith itself is among the gifts grace works in the person; it is not credited as an unaided achievement of the will.
The image is wounded and darkened, not simply erased — yet without grace the will does not use it aright for God.
